cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), says the plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD (Proverbs 16:1). Man brings the plan, and the reply comes from the LORD. I plan a whole batch in my head, and then I open my mouth and something else entirely comes out. Humans plan, friends, and I'm the proof.

The answer is True. Solomon says all a man's ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD (Proverbs 16:2). Everybody's own scale says they're doing great. I once stamped a cookie so crooked it looked like a map of a lake, and I still called it art.

The answer is to commit your works to the LORD. Solomon says, "Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved." (Proverbs 16:3). Hand the work over to Him and the promise comes with it. Short instruction, big promise, and no manual.

The answer is that they will not go unpunished. Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD, and Solomon says to be assured that he will not go unpunished (Proverbs 16:5). It's a serious line, so I'll just say it plainly, friends. The proud heart doesn't get a pass.

The answer is by the fear of the LORD. Solomon says that by loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil (Proverbs 16:6). Loving devotion and faithfulness are the first half, and the fear of the LORD is the second. Two halves, like a cookie snapped down the middle.

The answer is True. When a man's ways please the LORD, He makes even the man's enemies live at peace with him (Proverbs 16:7). Even the enemies, friends. That's a promise bigger than any seating chart at a family cookout.

The answer is a little with righteousness. Solomon says, "Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice." (Proverbs 16:8). The small pile with righteousness beats the big pile with injustice. I'll take a half-empty cookie box I earned honestly over a full one I shouldn't have.

The answer is steps. A man's heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps (Proverbs 16:9). The heart draws the map and the LORD determines the steps. I never planned on a cookie planet, friends, and yet here I am on a gold base with a mustache full of flour.

The answer is False. Solomon says honest scales and balances are from the LORD, and "all the weights in the bag are His concern." (Proverbs 16:11). Every weight in the bag is His concern. Honest weights matter to Him.

The answer is righteousness. Wicked behavior is detestable for kings, for a throne is established through righteousness (Proverbs 16:12). A throne stands on righteousness, friends. It isn't built on a pile of cheating.

The answer is wise. The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it (Proverbs 16:14). The wise man calms it down. Walking into a room with an angry king and leaving calm takes real wisdom.

The answer is a rain cloud in spring. When a king's face brightens, there is life, and his favor is like a rain cloud in spring (Proverbs 16:15). A spring rain cloud means good things are on the way. A king's favor is welcome like that.

The answer is away from evil. Solomon says, "The highway of the upright leads away from evil…" and adds that he who guards his way protects his life (Proverbs 16:17). The upright keep traveling away from evil. That's a highway worth staying on, friends.

The answer is fall. Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall (Proverbs 16:18). Pride walks in first and a fall follows. I once strutted across my bakery like I owned the place and slid face-first into the chocolate chips.

The answer is False. Solomon says, "It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud." (Proverbs 16:19). Being lowly among the humble beats a share of the spoil with the proud. A smaller seat with good company is the better one, friends.

The answer is he who trusts in the LORD. Solomon says whoever heeds instruction will find success, "…and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD." (Proverbs 16:20). The blessed one is the one who trusts. Trust is the word to hold onto here, friends.

The answer is folly. Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly (Proverbs 16:22). A fountain of life on one side and folly on the other. Solomon sets the two side by side so you can see the difference.

The answer is True. Solomon says, "The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips." (Proverbs 16:23). The heart teaches the mouth what to say. That's a mouth with good training.

The answer is a honeycomb. Solomon says, "Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones." (Proverbs 16:24). A kind word does good for the whole person, soul and bones. That's a lot for a few words to do, friends. Pleasant words are worth handing out.

The answer is death, and it's a heavy one. "There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death." (Proverbs 16:25). The way only seems right, friends. Its end is the way of death.

The answer is True. Solomon says a worker's appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward (Proverbs 16:26). The hunger does some of the pushing. It's why the oven opens early at my place.

The answer is that a gossip divides close friends. Solomon says, "A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends." (Proverbs 16:28). Close friends are the ones who get split. Gossip is a small thing that does big damage.

The answer is down a path that is not good. A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good (Proverbs 16:29). He doesn't stay on the path alone, friends. He takes his neighbor with him.

The answer is True. Gray hair is a crown of glory, and Solomon says it is attained along the path of righteousness (Proverbs 16:31). It's a glad line in a chapter with some heavy ones. The crown comes along that path.

The answer is warrior. Solomon says, "He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city." (Proverbs 16:32). Controlling your temper is called greater than capturing a city. It's harder than it sounds, friends, especially when the oven door slams on your mustache.

The answer is the LORD. Solomon says, "The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD." (Proverbs 16:33). It looks like chance, but every decision of the lot is from Him. A lot was a way of making a choice by casting it.
